title: Identifying DNA Damage Responders via Proximity Biotinylation of PCNA Interactors
author: Borosta, Szepesi-Nagy, et al.

steps.title: Prepare workspace and safety gear
steps.instruction: Wear gloves, a face mask, safety goggles, and a head cover; work in a clean bench; use only pre‑sterilized, protein‑free tubes that have not been opened.

steps.title: Resuspend streptavidin beads
steps.instruction: Mix the MyOne C1 Streptavidin Magnetic Beads stock thoroughly to obtain a uniform slurry before use.

steps.title: Aliquot beads and add buffer
steps.instruction: Transfer 25 µL streptavidin bead slurry per sample (equivalent to 25 µL per 15 cm plate) into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube and add 1 mL RIPA IP buffer; adjust proportionally for multiple plates (e.g., 4 plates → 100 µL beads in 250 µL buffer).

steps.title: Collect beads magnetically
steps.instruction: Place the tube in a magnetic stand, wait ~2 min for beads to gather on the tube side, then carefully remove and discard the supernatant without allowing beads to dry.

steps.title: Resuspend beads in buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the bead pellet in 250 µL RIPA IP buffer, ensuring the bead volume matches the number of 15 cm plates used (e.g., 4 plates → 100 µL beads in 250 µL buffer).

steps.title: Add beads to chromatin lysate
steps.instruction: Combine the 250 µL bead suspension with the 950 µL chromatin fraction prepared in Step 25, mixing gently.

steps.title: Incubate beads with lysate
steps.instruction: Rotate the tube end‑over‑end at 4 °C for 2–3 h, keeping at least 1 mL total volume in the tube to avoid protein precipitation; avoid foaming and do not let beads dry.

steps.title: Wash beads twice with RIPA
steps.instruction: Perform two washes with 1 mL RIPA IP buffer each: place tube on magnetic stand until beads collect, remove supernatant with a P1000 pipette, add 1 mL RIPA IP buffer, and repeat.

substeps.instruction: Place tube on magnetic stand and wait for beads to collect

steps.title: High‑salt wash beads
steps.instruction: Wash beads once with 1 mL high‑salt RIPA IP buffer containing 500 mM NaCl, using the same magnetic‑stand procedure to remove non‑specific Histone H1 binding.

steps.title: Wash without inhibitors (first)
steps.instruction: Wash beads once with 1 mL RIPA IP buffer that lacks Complete ULTRA protease tablet and PhosSTOP phosphatase inhibitors, to keep the final eluate free of these reagents.

steps.title: Transfer beads to fresh tube
steps.instruction: Optionally move the bead slurry to a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube to reduce background contamination.

steps.title: Final wash without inhibitors
steps.instruction: Wash beads once more with 1 mL RIPA IP buffer that does not contain protease or phosphatase inhibitors.

steps.title: Elute proteins from beads
steps.instruction: Resuspend beads in 150 µL Elution buffer and heat at 95 °C for 10 min to release bound biotinylated proteins.

steps.title: Collect eluate and store
steps.instruction: Place tubes on a magnetic rack, transfer the supernatant (eluate) to a fresh tube, discard the beads, and store eluates at –80 °C for up to 6 months before mass‑spectrometry analysis.

description: The following protocol outlines a step-by-step procedure for applying proximity labeling to investigate the interactome of chromatin bound proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) in living cells. In our study, we employed this approach in G1-synchronized RPE1 cells to characterize PCNA-associated proteins in response to oxidative DNA damage.1 However, the protocol is highly versatile and can be readily adapted to other cell types, proximity labeling targets, and genotoxic stress conditions. It is also compatible with asynchronous cell populations or cells synchronized at other phases of the cell cycle, enabling broader exploration of dynamic protein interactions across various biological contexts.
